task.description:
Write test specs and test code for REQ-373 per WF-02 Step 3's procedure (docs/agents/workflows/WF-02_requirement_implementation.md), covering EVERY one of REQ-373's 8 acceptance criteria (task.acceptance_criteria below). Read lib/letflow/design/req373-service-catalog-version-lifecycle.md and the implementation files in artifacts_in first. Write test/specs/req373-service-catalog-version-lifecycle.md (requirement text, test cases, why each exists) and test code under test/letflow/ (or test/letflow_web/ for API-layer tests), following the property-test convention already established elsewhere in this project where applicable.

Specifically required test cases (do not treat this list as exhaustive -- add more if a real gap exists, but these are mandatory): (1) a schema/migration test proving service_catalog entries carry a version identity + ACTIVE/RETIRED status (AC1); (2) the TWO-SIDED retire test -- a fresh resolve/4 call against a retired ref FAILS (not falls through), AND PinResolver.pin_for/3 against an already-pinned instance whose pin references the now-retired version continues to resolve with NO error (AC4) -- this is the single most important test in this run, make sure both halves are genuinely exercised, not just one; (3) the publish-doesn't-disturb-pinned test: resolve a pin, publish a new version of the same service_id, re-derive the same instance's effective pin set and assert it is UNCHANGED (AC2); (4) a test that a NEW case created after a publish resolves the newly published version via PinResolver.resolve/4's real Lookup (AC3); (5) the Engine.create/2 INTEGRATION test: start a real instance referencing a SERVICE_TASK's service_id and confirm a :resolved (not :unresolved_catalog_ref-failing) pin is recorded, proving the real Lookup is actually wired in at the call site, not just unit-tested in isolation (AC5); (6) the :AdminServicesManage permission-gate test for both new publish/retire routes -- confirm a caller without that permission is rejected and a caller with it succeeds (AC6); (7) confirm no test needs to cover PLC-01/module_ref (AC7 is a moduledoc-citation check, not a test-code check -- do not invent a test for it).

Do not run the tests yourself (TEST-RUNNER's job). Verify: every acceptance criterion has >=1 test case that would fail if violated; no test depends on wall-clock time or unseeded randomness; test fixtures use per-test unique data. Complete the handoff with artifacts_out listing every file written, next_action 'Route to TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR'. Commit and push (explicit filenames, never -A) to origin feature/WF02-REQ373-20260921 before ending your turn.
acceptance_criteria: service_catalog entries carry a version identity and an ACTIVE/RETIRED status, with the chosen schema (composite key vs. status+sibling table) stated explicitly in the moduledoc along with the reasoning, proven by a migration and a schema test

publishing a new version of an existing service_id does not alter or invalidate any already-resolved pinned_version entry recorded in a prior INSTANCE_STARTED event, proven by a test that resolves a pin, publishes a new version, and re-derives the same instance's effective pin set unchanged
a new case created after a publish resolves the newly published version via Letflow.Engine.PinResolver.resolve/4's real (non-default) Lookup, proven by a test

retiring a version prevents any NEW resolution from choosing it (a fresh resolve/4 call against the retired ref fails or falls through to the current version, whichever this requirement's own design specifies -- stated explicitly, not left ambiguous) while an instance already pinned to the retired version continues to resolve via pin_for/3 with no error, proven by a test covering both sides

Engine.create/2's pin_lookup/2 helper is wired to the real catalog-backed Lookup for catalog_entry references in place of PinResolver.default_lookup/0, proven by an integration test that starts a real instance referencing a SERVICE_TASK's service_id and confirms a :resolved (not :unresolved_catalog_ref-failing) pin is recorded
publish/retire operations are gated behind the already-shipped :AdminServicesManage permission (Letflow.Api.Authorization), not a newly invented permission name, proven by a test

PLC-01/module_ref catalog versioning is explicitly named as still out of scope in the moduledoc, with a citation of pin_resolver.ex's own existing SCOPE GAP language, not silently expanded into this requirement's scope
mix letflow.check passes, with real output quoted
